solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Golf club: Irish one, not English

indicators.note: not English says the letter standing for English is left out of what comes before

parts.note: taken as the word itself

explanation.surface: A golfer describes a club as Irish in origin rather than English.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not English' removes the E from IR + ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: An iron is one of the metal-headed clubs a golfer carries in the bag.

clue.text: Pick out deity if name initially bandied about

indicators.note: bandied about means tossed around, so the letters that precede are mixed into a new order
initially means just the opening letter of the word name is used

parts.note: its first letter N

explanation.surface: Someone singles out a god whose name has been carelessly spread around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes N from 'name'; 'bandied about' rearranges DEITY + IF + N.
explanation.definitionFit: To identify a suspect is to pick them out from a line-up; the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Being broadcast? Extract from Wagnerian opera coming up

indicators.note: coming up says the hidden letters are read backwards, as this is a down clue
an extract is a passage lifted from a longer text, so the answer lies inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A radio presenter asks whether a passage from a Wagner opera is being broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Extract' into the definition, but 'Extract from' is what signals the hidden letters RIANO in wagneRIAN Opera; 'coming up' reverses them.
explanation.definitionFit: A programme that is on air is currently being transmitted to listeners or viewers.

clue.text: Pleasure-seeker's complaint involving a bad back

indicators.note: involving means the complaint wraps round the letters that follow

parts.note: gout is a painful illness, a complaint in the medical sense

indicators.note: back says the word bad is written in reverse

parts.note: taken as written before reversal

explanation.surface: A hedonist suffers an ailment that includes a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: Gout is a painful swelling of the joints, often the big toe. The 's stands for 'has', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadabout flits from one social amusement to the next, a habitual seeker after fun.

clue.text: Provider of beef under an age BSE affected

indicators.note: affected here means altered or disturbed, so the preceding letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cattle below a certain age have been hit by mad cow disease.
explanation.walkthrough: BSE is bovine spongiform encephalopathy, 'mad cow disease', which badly hit British beef herds in the 1990s.
explanation.definitionFit: Aberdeen Angus is a Scottish breed of cattle reared chiefly for its meat.

clue.text: Accumulate a large amount

parts.note: a mass is a great quantity of something

explanation.surface: Gather together a great deal.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather or pile up over time, the same as building a store.

clue.text: Rotten worker, curt

parts.note: food that has gone off is rotten
a hand is a manual worker, as in farmhand

explanation.surface: A boss dismisses a decaying employee with a brusque remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An offhand manner is brusque and casual, lacking courtesy, just like a short reply.

clue.text: Informed, foremost of teachers getting on in years

indicators.note: foremost of picks out only the leading letter of the following word

parts.note: its first letter T
someone getting on in years is old

explanation.surface: Elderly senior teachers have been briefed.
explanation.definitionFit: Informed and told are both past forms meaning having passed on news to someone.

clue.text: Choose not to participate in work with aggressive solicitor?

parts.note: OP is short for opus, a work
a tout pesters people to buy, as with ticket touts

explanation.surface: Someone declines to take part in a job alongside a pushy lawyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a British lawyer, but here it means one who solicits custom.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt out is to withdraw by choice from a scheme or activity.

clue.text: Former partner given sufficient warning

parts.note: an ex is a former spouse or partner
ample means plenty, enough

explanation.surface: Someone's ex was given plenty of notice.
explanation.definitionFit: A punishment made an example of serves as a deterrent caution to others.

clue.text: Terrible just losing face

indicators.note: losing face means the word drops its front letter, its face

parts.note: lawful means just, in accordance with law

explanation.surface: A dreadful situation where someone is simply humiliated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'just' looks like 'merely' but is the adjective meaning fair.
explanation.definitionFit: Awful and terrible are synonyms meaning extremely bad.

clue.text: Some actors opening trunk

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Several performers are unpacking a large travelling chest.
explanation.definitionFit: The trunk is the body without head or limbs, which is the anatomical torso.

clue.text: Miserable maids, mistreated, left

indicators.note: mistreated means handled badly, so the letters of maids are jumbled

explanation.surface: Unhappy housemaids, badly treated, have quit.
explanation.definitionFit: Dismal means gloomy and depressing, a close synonym for miserable.

clue.text: Unsophisticated fictional detective picked up play on words

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the detective's name is given by its sound

parts.note: Sherlock Holmes, Conan Doyle's detective
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A storybook sleuth caught a simple joke.
explanation.walkthrough: HOLMES is pronounced with a silent L, so it sounds like HOMES.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and simple, without polish, like cloth woven at home.

clue.text: How Monopoly starts, as it always has?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: play in the board game Monopoly begins from the square marked GO
second meaning: right from the very beginning

explanation.walkthrough: Monopoly is the property-trading board game whose starting square reads GO.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means since the outset, and literally describes leaving the GO square at the start of play.

clue.text: Leader of Opposition helping to produce speech

indicators.note: leader of takes just the opening letter of the word that follows

parts.note: its first letter O
a ration is a portion, a helping

explanation.surface: The head of the Opposition party is assisting with a speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Leader of Opposition' looks like a political title, but only the first letter is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal public address, a kind of speech.

clue.text: Old theologian followed by boy most likely to succeed

indicators.note: followed by means the next piece comes after the earlier ones

parts.note: DD is Doctor of Divinity, a theologian
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: An elderly cleric has his son coming next, the favourite to win.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse that is odds-on is the betting favourite, expected to win.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts, mostly

indicators.note: mostly means nearly all of the word, with its final letter dropped

parts.note: bananas is slang for crazy, nuts

explanation.surface: A mix of fruit and nuts, chiefly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nuts' looks like the food, but it means mad.
explanation.definitionFit: The banana is a long yellow tropical fruit.

clue.text: Article upset stage show's backer

parts.note: an is the indefinite article

indicators.note: upset means turned over, so in this down clue the word is written from bottom to top

parts.note: a leg is a stage of a journey or race

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece annoyed a theatre's financier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stage' suggests theatre, but means a leg, as of a relay, reversed to GEL.
explanation.definitionFit: An angel is theatre slang for an investor who funds a production.

clue.text: Former chief magistrate imprisoning duke for deception

indicators.note: imprisoning means the first word holds the next inside it

parts.note: the doge was the elected chief magistrate of Venice or Genoa

explanation.surface: An old Venetian ruler jailed a nobleman by trickery.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodge is a trick or ruse, a piece of cunning deceit.

clue.text: Slow learner expected to take in new chapter

indicators.note: to take in means the first word encloses the following letters

parts.note: a baby that is due is expected

explanation.surface: A weak pupil is supposed to absorb a fresh chapter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dunce is a pupil who struggles to learn, a dullard.

clue.text: Crooked scheme rascal detailed

indicators.note: detailed means de-tailed, the word losing its last letter

parts.note: a scamp is a mischievous rascal

explanation.surface: A villain set out a dishonest plan in full.
explanation.walkthrough: 'detailed' reads as 'described fully' but splits as de-tailed: tail removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A scam is a fraudulent ploy, a dishonest racket.

clue.text: Cold fish? Hold on!

parts.note: C is the tap abbreviation for cold
ling is a long cod-like sea fish

explanation.surface: Someone describes a distant person, then cries out to wait.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cold fish' looks like an unfriendly person, but it splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To cling is to grip tightly and not let go; the exclamation reads as an imperative telling someone to keep their grip.

clue.text: Adult's complaint heard and raised

indicators.note: heard means the word is given by how it sounds

parts.note: a groan is a moan of complaint
up means raised

explanation.surface: A grown person's grumble was both audible and lifted.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A grown-up is a person who has reached maturity, an adult.

clue.text: Famous painting in oils a man vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised means damaged, so the letters before it are wrecked into a new order

explanation.surface: A man defaced a celebrated oil painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo's portrait in the Louvre is perhaps the world's best-known artwork.

clue.text: Represent chaps holding answer

indicators.note: holding says the first word keeps the following letter inside it

parts.note: chaps are men

explanation.surface: Fellows are keeping hold of a reply.
explanation.definitionFit: To mean is to signify or stand for, as a symbol represents something.
